definition: The proportion of positive predictions made by a model that are actually correct.
details: Precision is especially important in settings where false positives are costly, such as spam detection or medical diagnosis screening.

explainer.lead: Precision is the share of a model's positive predictions that are actually correct. It matters most where false positives are expensive.

tiers.eli5: If you flag ten emails as spam and only seven really are spam, your precision is seven out of ten.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use precision when evaluating models whose false positives carry a real cost. A pitfall is optimizing precision alone, which says nothing about positives the model missed.
tiers.paperLevel: Precision = correct positive predictions / all positive predictions; it measures only the positive class and does not capture false negatives.

explainer.example: In medical diagnosis screening, a screen flagging many healthy patients as positive would have low precision, and each false positive is costly.
